body:
> Overall, profile guided optimization may be a much better approach of achieving similar/better gains by rooting the compiler choices into real usage data. But I have no idea on how to even start with that :D

I don't think that's true. A profile would need to use every feature that we need to be fast in a single profile, i.e. a benchmark that spans all our performance critical features. This is not feasible.
Any features not covered by the benchmark would get a call count of 0, and be optimized for size instead of speed, against our intention. 

I did consider an approach where we auto-generate a fake profile by simply marking the features we need to be fast as "called often", but this would be a lot of work, and it wouldn't be any better than adding `_COLD_` where it's needed.

So I ended up with the same design as this PR in my head, just hadn't pushed a PR for it.

> Unfortunately this does nothing on macOS, and even marking every `_bind_methods` / `_bind_compatibility_methods` with `_COLD_` only grows size by ~600kb. Probably because it interferes with the machine outliner.

I did some tests a couple of weeks ago and with `_COLD_` on every `_bind_methods`, I saved 2 MiB off the `template_release` for Linux Clang. But yeah it may not work the same on macOS.
Here's the branch implementing that approach: https://github.com/akien-mga/godot/tree/size-cold-init-perclass

> I'm also measuring a binary size increase on web, even with brotli.

How much? In a previous test I had +20 KiB on Web, which isn't terrible. It likes comes just from the added method in `GDCLASS` as there's now both `_initialize_class` and `_initialize_class_cold` (and the former may still get inlined). Web builds with `-Os` by default so it already solves the problem we're trying to fix by not inlining most of this stuff.

I retested now and it still works for me with Clang for Linux builds **with LTO** (3.63 MB reduction on the editor, almost exactly the same as I measured with GCC). If you tested on macOS without LTO, you would indeed not see much gain.

```
-rwxr-xr-x. 1 akien akien 152.27MiB Oct 16 10:42 godot.linuxbsd.editor.x86_64.llvm.code-init-perclass.lto
-rwxr-xr-x. 1 akien akien 135.85MiB Oct 16 10:34 godot.linuxbsd.editor.x86_64.llvm.code-init-perclass.nolto
-rwxr-xr-x. 1 akien akien 155.90MiB Oct 16 09:56 godot.linuxbsd.editor.x86_64.llvm.master.lto
-rwxr-xr-x. 1 akien akien 136.18MiB Oct 16 10:27 godot.linuxbsd.editor.x86_64.llvm.master.nolto
```

Yes, just a regular macOS `clang` build, so no LTO.

Since LTO is currently increasing binary size on mac, but only by a few megabytes, but improves performance on benchmarks ~5%, we should definitely consider switching macOS to LTO after this

To recap the findings so far:

> With GCC, this PR saves **2.40 MiB** on a Linux `template_release` (**-3.2%**) and **3.60 MiB** on a Linux `editor` (**-2.8%**).

GCC is the only compiler that really benefits from the PR as it stands, thanks to it propagating coldness to callees which are only used in cold functions.

Worth noting that those gains with this minimal diff depend on the functions we want to infer as cold to only be called from functions marked as cold, which is the case now with all the chain of class init and bindings, and called through `Main`.

> It only saves 0.88 MiB (-1.1%) on Windows mingw-gcc, but that may be partially caused by a workaround we have now which seems to limit LTO efficiency, which I'll look into.

I looked into this, and the smaller gains are due to #103077 which disabled some of the gains we would expect from LTO. It's not directly related to this `cold` change, and more the sign that we're leaving a lot of size reduction on the table due to this workaround (I measured 12.4 MiB reduction on `master` by reverting this workaround).

We started looking into this again in https://chat.godotengine.org/channel/buildsystem?msg=47Hndd6iEBhwRTutW which may lead to us fixing the bug in GCC so we can undo the workaround and reap the benefits again.

This will make this PR also benefit Windows mingw-gcc builds with a similar size reduction to Linux GCC.

> With Clang on Linux, it only saves ~70 KiB.

Clang doesn't propagate coldness the same way GCC does, so if we want the same benefits, we need to flag each `_bind_methods` and `register*` declaration as `_COLD_`. That's easily doable but increases the diff size a lot:

https://github.com/akien-mga/godot/tree/size-cold-init-perclass

And this would need to be documented so new classes do the same.
This would bring the size reduction for Clang to the same level as GCC, which would benefit Android, macOS, and iOS presumably. Still no gain for Web which is already optimized for size.

> With Emscripten, it very slightly increases the wasm size (20 KiB, +0.06%).

While unfortunate, I think this is negligible. Web is already optimized for size so this PR doesn't provide any benefits, and the split of `_initialize_class` into two methods carries a bit of extra weight it seems.

---

Overall, I'd say the diff is minimal and the GCC gains are an easy win, so this could be mergeable.
